status: REGISTERED. Requested by the author on 2026-10-25 ('go, can you find if my new paper is worth or not with simulation'). Pushed in a commit of its own before the registered seeds 1001-1100 were run.
designed_after: An exploratory pilot on seeds 101-110 (control, fast and slow vendor scenarios; window 10 days; warning rules lost, buffer 0.1 and time-to-zero 10 days): no false alarms of the standard estimator in 10 controls; standard time-to-zero median lead 9.5 days (fast) and 19 days (slow); disclosed buffer median lead 15.5 days against 1 day for the standard buffer in the slow scenario; disclosed time-to-zero false alarms in 10 of 10 controls (not used). One run on seed 105 showed the adoption share at the crisis (0.38) far below the static monoculture threshold (0.83); selftests used seeds 1 and 2.
question: In a simulated market of learning agents adopting a shared vendor model, does the thesis's public-data certificate warn before instability without false alarms, does disclosing a memory bound buy warning time when the shared model is slow, and does learning make monoculture dangerous at a lower adoption share than static analysis predicts?
seeds: 1001-1100 for each of the scenarios control, fast (r_D = 0.9), slow (r_D = 0.995); 300 runs of 120 days
primary_1: specificity: the standard estimator's time-to-zero rule fires in at most 5 of the 100 control runs
primary_2: early warning: over the fast and slow runs with a crisis, the standard time-to-zero rule fires before the crisis in at least 80% (one-sided binomial p < 0.05) with median lead at least 5 days
primary_3: disclosure: in the slow runs with a crisis, the disclosed estimator's buffer warning precedes the standard one (exact one-sided sign test p < 0.05) with median gain at least 5 days
primary_4: learning accelerates monoculture: the adoption share at the crisis is below the static threshold of Proposition prop:monoculture (learners frozen at the start of adoption) in at least 75% of runs with a crisis (one-sided binomial p < 0.05)
correction: Holm across primaries 2-4 at 0.05; primary 1 is a pass/fail criterion
secondary: false alarms of every rule and estimator in the controls
median leads by scenario, rule and estimator
median tracking error |M_hat - M_true| on days with M_true > 0.2
median share at crisis and median static threshold
share of ramp runs with a crisis
limits_stated_in_advance: a simulation: the agents are simple learning rules and a fixed momentum product, not language-model agents or real bank systems
adoption is exogenous and ramps linearly
the observer sees the true displacement, not a moving-average proxy
the crisis definition and warning thresholds were chosen in the pilot
